151021.overview:
Internet's gone!
Ohh ... What is that?
A dinosario.
In an era where the advance of the video game industry seems to be measured by the number of frames per second, the number of polygons displayed on the screen or the width in pixels with names like HD, HD ready, Full HD, Ultra HD, 4k and Retina Display (because the aspect of the 16: 9 screen is very mainstream) it is very difficult to expect that a multi-billion dollar company like Google would go against the trends.

T-Rex Runner, also known as "The only thing left to do when going to the Internet," is a game that has all the global capacity with access to a computer but that has never been given the time for analysis and appreciation.
That is why there is a way of retro-analysis, here I leave the review of T-Rex Runner exclusively for Google Chrome.

Join me to live this sad story.
Let's start talking about the theme of the game. A simple view of a Tyrannosaurus Rex running from left to right that points to blocks as segments of small sizes, groups or groups, while earning points for each meter that it does. but the premise goes far beyond just that.

T-Rex Runner presents a tragic unit in a situation where there is no way to win.

T-Rex Runner represents a sad story based on the primary need of almost every living being (with the exception of the Lemores and the members of My Chemical Romance) to preserve their life against any kind of danger, even when tragic outcome is completely inevitable .

Our hero, Rex, is not running alone because he likes to exercise every morning, he runs terrified. Let's think then, if the character is nothing more and nothing less than the king of the dinosaurs and one of the most powerful carnivores (or scavengers, and no one agrees) of history. What could cause so much terror? The answer is simple: Extinction.

167278.overview: This is an unusual platformer where you have to tilt the level to move the player. There are 20 levels that get progressively harder

219232.overview: Trollface Launch takes the typical gameplay of flight simulation Flash games, in which you launch your character, earning money based on distance and using that money to buy upgrades in order to fly farther, with a twist! The game uses the Trollface, officially licensed from the creator, and has all sorts of troll-y shenanigans in the game.

219493.overview:
Teen Titans Battle Blitz is an online Shockwave 2-D fighting game released in 2003 by THIS IS POP for Cartoon Network to coincide with and promote the launch of the series.

The game takes place around the episodes: "Final Exam" and "Divide and Conquer".

422666.overview: With over 40 levels, over 60 characters, over 3 minutes worth of cutscenes, over 2 months of development, over 9000 jokes, over $153 spent on coffee, and over 6 statistics made up, you'd think I'd have a better title.

451484.overview:
Thing-Thing Arena is the third game in the Thing-Thing series to be released, as well as the first spin-off game (with the exception of The Chronicles of Stinky Bean).

Unlike in Thing-Thing 2, where you have to get to the end of the level and killing some enemies along the way, Thing-Thing Arena has you going up against endless waves of enemies in an enclosed area. It features four gameplay modes:
- Survival Mode: It has returned from Thing-Thing 2, and this time, you have to fight off as many enemies as you can before you die. But this time, the enemies are armed with guns and can fire at you, and the difficulty progresses as your number of kills grow.
- Zombie Survival: A new twist on Survival Mode, where you face zombified enemies that move faster and drop less health pick-ups. You also start with less health, as well, but don't worry, you'll have a nigh-infinite supply of ammo in your "Zombie Special" (a Franchi SPAS-12 shotgun).
- Super Survival: A tougher version of the standard Survival Mode, where the enemies come with stronger weapons. In addition, your starting loadout also comes with a Gyrojet with 20 rockets and a Milkor MGL with 30 grenades.
- Stinky Bean Survival: The game also marks the first appearance of the "world's most pathetic lifeform", the Stinky Bean. Even though they're not armed with guns, they're still a threat in numbers. Make sure you have enough, because these guys are going to spawn fast.

451485.overview: Thy Dungeonman 3 (also spelled Thy Dungeonman III) is the second sequel in the Thy Dungeonman franchise produced by Videlectrix. The most notable feature of this sequel is the addition of graphics, with imitation low-resolution still frames accompanying each room of the game. As with the first two installments in the Thy Dungeonman series, the game is a text-command-controlled adventure centered around a knight named Thy Dungeonman. However, the mission in this quest is to get Ye Flask, rather than to escape yon dungeon as in the previous games.

451486.overview:
Amidst the hustle and bustle of an urban street intersection, an alley cat (controlled with the mouse) tries to forage for something tasty and sustaining. Pedestrians throng in and out of the crosswalks continually, and often a delectable container of take-out will just be abandoned in the middle of the road. The objective is to move and maneuver the cat to the food before a counter (measuring freshness, perhaps?) ticks down from 1000 to 100, indicating the amount of points it is worth to the cat. No big problem, save that if the cat makes contact with a pedestrian, the game is over. This can be managed using an unusual strategic dynamic, pedestrians only moving while the cat does.

Periodically a power-up will appear, a white ball, allowing the cat to emit a circle that repels pedestrians. This is invoked by clicking the mouse, but they are few and far between. A maximum of three of the power-ups can be stockpiled, but progressive gameplay ensures that pedestrian density will only increase as the game goes on.

451487.overview:
Tetrageddon is a collection of games, strange rabbit holes, tangents, and a comedic digital nightmare about the internet of old.
It is a bizarre relic from the era of online Flash games, and pretty much delivers on as random of an experience as you would expect.
Each game is wildly different in terms of genre and gameplay. They all have their own silly tangents and Easter eggs to explore. You can spend hours getting lost.

Explore haunted desktops and abandoned spaces as you delve deeper into a pixelated fever dream. On your journey you will encounter silly characters and other oddities while you brave what feels like someone’s long forgotten games folder on a computer found during a garage sale.

Tetrageddon is a satire about our digital culture in the form of a strange collection of mini games. If you like random humor, warioware, miss the days of Flash game portals and the weird trappings of 90's nostalgia... then Tetrageddon is for you!

There are a total of ten mini-games that you can uncover. These range from Anatomically Incorrect Dinosaurs, a dinosaur assembly simulator... to Froggy (It's Hungry!), a post-apocalyptic game about a frog surviving on an international mega-highway at the end of the world.
Tetrageddon is the type of game that's hard to describe and best experienced for yourself.

451501.overview:
This Is The Only Level is a single-screen platformer similar to Achievement Unlocked, in which the player controls an elephant in a room full of floating platforms and spikes.

Unlike the elephant's previous game, the goal is to get the elephant from the pipe at the top of the screen to the pipe at the bottom of the screen. As the title implies, there is only one level, but that level consists of thirty stages, each with a different method of completion but mostly revolving around pressing a large button that opens a door behind which the exit pipe is hidden.

451515.overview:
Welcome to the first puppet show RPG! Participate in battling a ton of foes, buy new upgrades, cast magic and recruit new Heroes. Or just sit back and enjoy the show as your Heroes fight on their own while you watch or do other things.

Features:
- Over 70 different enemies and bosses
- 10 different areas
- A Distinct group of heroes with different abilities
- Interesting powers to unleash on your enemies
- Mix of RPG and clicker grind elements with tons of skills to upgrade
- No microtransactions of any sort
- Possibly infinite gameplay
- Puppet stage graphics with cute puppet heroes!

451516.overview:
Territory WAR is a turn-based strategy game inspired by the popular series of games Worms.

In this game's default gamemode, the player controls multiple stick figures in their turn and can move or stand still. After moving or choosing to stand still, the player can choose 4 different offensive options. These options include: 1 - Grenade: Causes splash damage to multiple enemies, while also throwing them away from the explosion. Damage and throw power depends on distance from the explosion. 2 - Gun: Causes significant damage especially if aimed at the head. Use it to kill single figures quickly. 3 - Boot: Melee attack that causes little damage but throws enemies very far. Useful for throwing enemies off-stage. Also causes splash damage, though it's radius of effect is much smaller than grenade's. 4 - Stand Still: Doesn't do anything and passes the turn. Use it if your figure is in a bad position and has nothing better to do.

The game has a Campaign mode where the player goes against the CPU in multiple different maps and with different numbers of stick figures, a Challenges mode where the player can test their aiming skills with grenades and guns while competing for the best scores online, and a Custom Battle mode where the player can play against a friend locally or against a CPU while choosing map and number of stick figures for both sides.

451517.overview:
TETRIS'D: The Game is an Avoid game by KobraEditing. It is based on his popular series of "T E T R I S ' D" animations, which is in turn based on the massively successfull game Tetris, created by Alexy Pajitnov and Vadim Gerasimov, originally for the Electronika 60.

Other than a brief tutorial, the player's only option is to play the main game with the aim of a high score. The player's goal is simple: their stick figure character must avoid being crushed by falling tetrads. The character is capable of the standard running and jumping found in most platforming games, and can be controlled using either the A, W, and D keys, or the arrow keys. However, the stickman also has two special moves. One, the Wall Jump, is activated using the J key. This will allow the player to jump off of the side of a tetrad while in air, and is useful for getting out of chasms. The second, the roll ability, is activated by the K key. This allows the player to grab onto a tetrad and roll up onto it. It allows the player to get out of harm's way much more easily than jumping.

451520.overview:
The story of Time Fcuk involves the protagonist being forced into a strange box by what appears to be himself from the future. Inside the box, there are multiple versions of him that communicate with him, some further along than him and some behind. Also while in the box, another person named Steven starts to grow out of his head and develop into what appears to be a twin of the protagonist before falling off and running away.

Gameplay in Time Fcuk consists of the player attempting to get to the exit portal. The player will have to move and stack boxes, collect keys, hold down switches, use warps, and manipulate gravity to get to the exit portal. The major gameplay mechanic in Time Fcuk involves switching the foreground with the background layer at will, while remaining in the same position. Moving between layers can be dangerous, since if you move into a space where a block is, you will kill your self. Certain blocks and platforms can be moved between layers by touching them when you switch. Additionally, some levels contain objects that will cause the layer to mirror either vertically or horizontally.

451522.overview:
Toss the Turtle is a Flash-based game, in which the player has to launch a turtle from a canon and make it travel as much distance as possible. While airborne, the turtle can be controlled with the WASD keys, either to be relaunched by letting it hit explosives or creatures, or to avoid obstacles like a spiked wall. The player also has a projectile weapon with limited ammunition, with which he can shoot the turtle up in the sky and a one-use jet pack.

After the flight, the player receives money, the amount being dependent on the distance travelled, objects hit, and money bags collected. This money can be used in the shop to upgrade the cannon, weapon or jet pack, or buy a chest bomb or nuclear thingy.

The game also sports achievements (e.g. having travelled a total of 50 miles) of which some give bonuses.

451687.overview: Windhawk is a flying action game. In this game, the player pilots a gyro copter armed to the brim with highly advanced military equipment. They can deploy and use the robotic cannon to target and destroy enemy air force invading air space.

451740.overview:
It's not like it’s a Point&Click that won the 2015 Construct Deception Jam, or that millions of people have tried it.
Of course not!
And if you’ve never heard of it, now’s the perfect time to go for a walk, read a book... or something…

Weak points:
- The voice-over acting is pathetic.
- There are only two different endings, which you’ll never even get to because you’re not going to install it.

480254.overview:
The First Cub is a 2D platformer with a great storytelling focus and varied gameplay that tries to push the limits of the Pico-8 engine.

The First is a member of an alien race called the "Bipterra", who was exiled from his tribe and rescued by a pair of scientists to test on him. Their motives seem unknown, whats only certain for The First is that they can't waste this chance.

Find out the truth behind the Bipterra and the E.G.
